abstract.p: This study proposes VisTRA (Visual Tool-use Reasoning Analyzer), a framework for analyzing how Visual Language Models (VLMs) utilize tools in Visual Question Answering (VQA) tasks involving small objects in highresolution images. While tools like object detection and zoom functionality are essential for small object VQA, their potential errors necessitate careful verification of outputs. Our framework provides systematic evaluation of VLMs' tool-use capabilities through analysis of verification patterns. Using the V* bench dataset, we find that direct acceptance of tool outputs correlates with decreased VQA accuracy, while lower-performing models exhibit higher frequencies of cyclic verification loops. These findings offer insights for improving tool verification mechanisms in VLM architectures focused on small object detection tasks.
